decision.rationale:
[recovery-agent diagnosis via claude-opus-5[1m]] No auto-remedy ran, correctly. The finding is BM_LADDER_NOT_CONVERGED with confidence=low: plateau_confirmed=true, and the only reason is loo_unstable. murnaghan_ladder_extend only fires at high confidence. assess_ladder_convergence (extract_bulk_modulus_murnaghan.py:210-250) marks leave-one-out alone as uncalibrated and meant for review, not for spending wall time. remedy_history holds only continue_npt x1 on cooling, so no mechanical rung has been spent.

Root cause: Murnaghan's constant K' is a poor fit over this ladder. It is not a ladder that is too narrow, and it is not undersampling.
(1) Only one LOO drop breaks the 10% threshold. Dropping 1 atm gives +13.65% (B0 2.148 GPa). The other five drops stay within 6.2%: 1000 -2.8%, 2500 +0.1%, 5000 -0.6%, 10000 -3.1%, 15000 -6.2%.
(2) The 1 atm point is not noise or drift. Its NPT volume samples every 50k steps scatter with no trend (96553-97895 A^3, reported mean 97323, SEM 46).
(3) Local secant moduli from the measured volumes, back-projected to P=0 with the fitted B0'=8.38, are: 0-1000 atm about 1.58 GPa; 1000-2500 about 1.96; 2500-5000 about 1.97; 5000-10000 about 1.77; 10000-15000 about 1.5. So K' falls with pressure. That fits a rubbery PE cell at 300 K (exp Tg 195 K) stiffening toward glass under compression; tau_frames drops to 1.0 at 10000 and 15000 atm.
Dropping the P~0 anchor forces the fit to extrapolate to V0 from high-pressure points that obey a different K'. That extrapolation is the 13.6% shift.

remedy_economics was not run. Mechanically it would return SPEND with spend_limit "one rung", because Class C with fewer than two history points always does. But the only lever it can price, bm_compression_limit_atm higher, points the wrong way here: the ladder-extend formula's next point would be 30000 atm. That adds a stiffer point further from the constant-K' regime and lengthens the extrapolation behind the instability. Densifying the low end with mechanical_resample_points=[500] is cheap (about 265 s of MD per point at 3600 UA atoms, lj_cut). It would only aim at the uncalibrated gate, though: I cannot show it clears 10%, and it would not change the best estimate. So revise_plan does not meet the confidence bar. retry does not apply because nothing here was transient.

The measured result is sound and should be accepted with an annotation by a human:
- K = 1.89 +/- 0.12 GPa (Murnaghan, BM_REPORTABLE, r^2=0.99987, 6 points, volume monotonic, B0'=8.38, inside the [4,20] band).
- Inside the plan's experimental band [1.5, 2.0] GPa.
- Cross-checked by the independent fluctuation estimator: 1.77 GPa, 6.28% divergence.

Carry this annotation: "LOO shift driven by P~0 anchor; K' decreases with P over the 1-15000 atm ladder (rubbery-to-stiffened crossover); Murnaghan B0 likely slightly high vs the low-P secant (1.58 GPa) and fluctuation (1.77 GPa) estimates; do not widen the ladder."

If the operator wants the gate cleared anyway, the one reasonable rung is mechanical_resample_points=[500] with mechanical_sampling_factor=1. Never raise the compression ceiling for this finding.

0: |dV/dP| between points 0 and 1 is 4.908, >3x the other intervals' median (1.356) -- possible cavitation/discontinuity in this interval.
1: |dV/dP| between points 0 and 1 is 4.908, >3x the other intervals' median (1.356) -- possible cavitation/discontinuity in this interval.

selected_window.selection_note: Untrimmed fit already has r_squared=0.99987 >= 0.999 -- no trimming applied even though point(s) [0, 1] were flagged (a genuinely curved EOS can trip the interval heuristic without a real problem).

warnings: Leave-one-out refit: dropping one pressure point shifts B0 by up to 13.6% (>10%) — the fit is not robust to a single point; consider widening the pressure range.

decision.rationale: [recovery-agent diagnosis via claude-opus-5[1m]] Transient GPU claim race, now resolved — the PROCESS_FAILED row's prescribed check ("look for a real cause — disk, GPU claim, host — before a blind retry") was done and the cause is identified and cleared. workflow_state.json shows remedy_counters.total=0 and agent_escalations=[], i.e. transient_retry's preflight (_transient_retry_blocked, workflow_engine.py:679) declined on len(free_gpus())<1 without spending either of its two applications. Timing is decisive: equilibration attempt-0001 was ACCEPTED at 21:52:14.963Z (plateau_equilibrated=true, drift 0.28%, n_effective=245) and cooling's claim failed 1.8 s later at 21:52:16.778Z. PE_1's equilibration chain ran on GPU 1 (data/_engine/run_state.json:357, "gpu_ids": "1"); cmd_release drops the lock instantly but free_gpus() also demands nvidia-smi idleness (util<=5%, mem<=800MB), so PE_1's own just-exited lmp still disqualified GPU 1 during CUDA-context teardown. As of now (21:54Z) pgrep -a lmp returns exactly two processes — PEEK_1 and PSU_1 — on GPUs 2 and 3, matching the only two locks in /tmp/polyjarvis/gpu_locks; no PolyJarvis process remains on GPU 0 or 1. Additional pressure came from an un-ledgered external tenant (PID 2231422, `python run.py --devices 0,1,2,3`, elapsed 1-02:30), but its per-GPU residency is intermittent, not permanent: PE_1 claimed GPU 1 successfully at 20:55 while that job was already ~25 h old, so it does not structurally block a claim. No decided_params key addresses GPU contention, so revise_plan has no correct lever; forcing engine=cpu/gpu_per_run=0 (viable at 3600 UA atoms, lj_cut, no PPPM) would rewrite hardware provenance and invalidate the admitted cost estimate mid-run — a human capacity call, not an auto-remedy. retry is bounded because transient_retry re-runs the disk+free-GPU preflight and declines rather than resubmitting blindly; the engine's own docstring records the 2026-09-08 case where three campaigns each wasted an escalation on a healthy retry wrongly declined. Caveat: GPUs 2-3 stay held by PEEK_1/PSU_1 (mid-equilibration, anneal_heat, stage 6/10) for hours alongside the external tenant, so a second PROCESS_FAILED here is sustained capacity exhaustion rather than a race and warrants stop/human scheduling, not a third attempt.

[recovery-agent diagnosis via claude-opus-5[1m]] Root cause: a momentary GPU-utilization spike by an un-ledgered external tenant, not capacity exhaustion, and not a defect in any decided_param. Evidence: (1) recovery_log.jsonl shows transient_retry declined at its own preflight at both 21:52:16 and 23:02:54 ("0 GPU(s) free, 1 needed"), and workflow_state.json remedy_counters.total=1 is entirely continue_npt:cooling — transient_retry's two applications are unspent, so this is NOT a third blind attempt. (2) /tmp/polyjarvis/gpu_locks holds only gpu2->PEEK_1 and gpu3->PSU_1; GPUs 0 and 1 are unclaimed, and pgrep -a lmp at 23:03:10 and 23:06 UTC returns only PEEK_1 and PSU_1 — no PolyJarvis process on 0 or 1. (3) cooling attempt-0003's npt_final_run.log last wrote 23:01:30 UTC and the claim failed at 23:02:54, 83 s later — too long for PE_1's own CUDA teardown, so the blocker is the neighbour (PID 2231422, `python run.py --devices 0,1,2,3`, 27 h elapsed). (4) The memory half of the claim test was already repaired: MIN_FREE_MEM_MB=8000 replaced the absolute 800 MB cap in commit bceab9f at 21:58:03 UTC, and _pick_gpu (run_campaign.py:124) invokes hardware_runtime.py as a fresh subprocess, so the 23:02:54 claim ran the fixed code; the remaining gate is util<=5% on a 40 GB A800 with ~34 GB free, i.e. a transient compute spike. (5) The neighbour's per-card residency is intermittent, not permanent: PE_1 claimed GPU 1 successfully at 20:55, 21:56 and 22:59 (the last two after that job was >25 h old) — 3 of 5 claims succeeded. Disk is not a co-cause (192 G free on /). This revises the prior escalation's caveat that a second PROCESS_FAILED implies sustained exhaustion: its premise was all four cards structurally occupied, but two successful GPU-1 claims have occurred since and the memory-side false negative was fixed in between; PEEK_1/PSU_1 holding 2 and 3 does not matter because PE_1 needs one of the two unclaimed cards. No decided_params key addresses GPU contention, so revise_plan has no correct lever — forcing engine=cpu/gpu_per_run=0 (feasible at ~3600 UA atoms, lj_cut, no PPPM) would rewrite hardware provenance and break the protocol lock this rev2 replicate campaign exists to set, a human capacity call. Caveat, stated plainly: nvidia-smi was denied in this headless session, so current util on GPUs 0/1 is inferred from the ledger, process table and log mtimes rather than read directly; the engine's transient_retry preflight re-checks free GPUs and declines rather than resubmitting into contention, and a failed claim costs ~1 s and lands in the same terminal escalation_required state that `stop` would produce immediately — so retry strictly dominates. Operator note: the claim is scoped per submission, so thermal->mechanical re-enters the same lottery with the escalation budget now spent.

operator_acceptance.why: The MEASUREMENT passed its own gate: bm_gate_verdict=BM_REPORTABLE, B0=1.8897 +/- 0.1198 GPa, B0'=8.3843, r^2=0.99987 over 6 monotonic points, inside the plan's experimental band [1.5, 2.0] GPa. What failed is a leave-one-out CONVERGENCE advisory that assess_ladder_convergence itself documents as uncalibrated and meant for review. The recovery agent returned action=stop rather than spend a rung, and recommended exactly this: accept with the annotation, and never widen the ladder for this finding.
